You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC: noisy-pixel cleanup task family

Observed solved instance `task-315375b1` (3 demos available; 2 demos used, 1 wrong submission). Rule: an otherwise regular grid scene contains one/two large solid-color shapes on a solid-color background, with scattered single-cell corruptions in unrelated colors. Remove the speckles by restoring each marked cell to the color implied by the underlying region/shape or to the background. Do not blanket-recolor all anomalies to background: some markers lie inside shape interiors and must be restored to that shape's color. Preserve all clean pixels and dimensions.

Evidence:
- Demo 1: background 0; regions 6, 2, 7; stray 5 pixels removed/restored; output retains only those scene colors and background.
- Demo 2: background 4; regions 5 and 8; many isolated anomalous colors (1,2,3,6,7,9) removed/restored; output retains 4/5/8 shapes.
- Solved test: background 1, regions 2 and 6; anomalous colors 3-9 restored according to the local shape/background pattern. A few markers inside shape regions (e.g. 5/9 in the 2-pattern, 7 within 6, 4 inside 2) must be shape-color, while outside speckles become 1.

Approach: identify background and coherent large regions first; treat isolated off-palette pixels as corrupted cells, then infer each replacement from the established local region/shape geometry, checking whether the cell is inside a shape versus background. The exact shape may be irregular, so avoid blindly filling a bounding box. In the solved case an initial guess incorrectly expanded an irregular 2-shape; a second demo clarified the general noise-cleanup rule, and correcting those cells solved it.
